chunks: Remember the favours He bestowed on you, and the covenant He cemented with you, when you said: 'We have heard and obey.' Have fear of God, for He knows the secrets of your heart.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'mithaq' in Surah Al-Ma'idah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the covenant of Al-Ghadir, where the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) established the authority of Imam Ali (AS) as the successor to the believers. The phrase 'We hear and we obey' (Sami'na wa Ata'na) is viewed as the believers' pledge of allegiance to this divine covenant, emphasizing both auditory acceptance and practical obedience. The reference to 'what is in the breasts' highlights the sincerity required in this covenant, distinguishing true faith from mere verbal declaration.
